about: The rules the cleanup engine decides without a disk, as cases both implementations answer.
`apps/desktop/src/mocks/cleanup.test.ts` runs the same cases through the mock's own two
functions. A rule that changes in one and not the other reddens a test here instead of
drifting quietly: the mock is the oracle every UI test of the Cleanup screen is written
against, and a mock that said yes to everything would make those tests prove nothing.
`items` are held by one module whose id is `test`. Each has one action, `go`, with the
options it lists; an option with `force: true` lifts a Keep verdict and no other does.
A `screen` case gives a request and expects `ok`, or the wire name of the `BlockReason`
that refuses it — rules 1 to 3 of the phase 2b design, section 8, in that order, the
first that applies deciding. A `reversible` case gives a plan as the kinds of its steps
(`delete`, `housekeeping`, `destroys`, `removes`) and says whether the Trash can undo it
Scope stops where a disk would be needed: the guards of a target, its kind, nesting across
a batch. Those are the guard cases' business and each side's own tests'.

screen.name: a safe item with no options passes
a review item passes: the confirmation is the glance a human was asked for
an item that is not held is missing
an item of a module nobody holds is missing too
an action the item does not offer: the item is not what the screen showed
an option the action does not have
one unknown option among known ones is enough
a keep item asked for with no options is kept
an option that is on but does not force leaves it kept
force beside another option lifts it just the same
an action with no force option cannot remove a keep item at all
force on an item that is not kept changes nothing
the first rule that applies decides: a missing item is missing, whatever it asks
an unknown action comes before the keep rule
an unknown option comes before the keep rule, even beside force

reversible.name: a folder to the Trash, then bookkeeping, the way a worktree goes
bookkeeping alone changes nothing a user could miss
a command that destroys: nothing about it goes to the Trash
a command that removes a path
one step the Trash cannot undo makes the whole entry so
